hints.title: Formulate as Net Zero Difference
hints.text: Choosing nums1[k] contributes +nums1[k] to the balance, while choosing nums2[k] contributes -nums2[k].

hints.title: Track Running Net Sums
hints.text: For each position, maintain a frequency map of reachable net sums from contiguous subarrays ending at that position.

hints.title: Transition and Count Balance Zero
hints.text: Either start a new subarray or extend all previous net sums by adding nums1[i] or subtracting nums2[i]. Accumulate the count of sum 0.

hints.title: Complete Python Solution
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def countSubranges(self, nums1: List[int], nums2: List[int]) -> int:
        MOD = 10**9 + 7
        dp = collections.defaultdict(int)
        ans = 0
        for x, y in zip(nums1, nums2):
            next_dp = collections.defaultdict(int)
            next_dp[x] = (next_dp[x] + 1) % MOD
            next_dp[-y] = (next_dp[-y] + 1) % MOD
            for s, count in dp.items():
                next_dp[s + x] = (next_dp[s + x] + count) % MOD
                next_dp[s - y] = (next_dp[s - y] + count) % MOD
            ans = (ans + next_dp[0]) % MOD
            dp = next_dp
        return ans
```

complexity.time: O(N) single pass or optimal algorithmic traversal
variables: N: input size or row count
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Evaluating every combination of 2^(j - i + 1) choices across all pairs (i, j) is super-exponential.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: DP with maximum sum S = 100 * 100 = 10000 takes O(N * S) time and O(S) auxiliary space.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Model signed balance in dynamic programming and take mod 10^9 + 7 at each transition.
